requirement:
Colon directive fences use three or more colons and support nested directives
with shorter inner fences. A colon-only closing fence has at least as many
colons as its opener, followed only by optional whitespace.
Backtick and tilde code fences follow CommonMark rules and shield their contents
from colon-directive recognition. Fence-like text in inline code or raw HTML
introduces no outline directive blocks.
rationale:
The five reviewed tests cover each clause of `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fence_precedence`. I found no gap.

**Colon fences of three or more colons, with nesting by shorter inner fences**
- `nested_fence_lengths_and_closer_whitespace_preserve_the_right_containers` nests a 4-colon `tip` block inside a 6-colon `note` block. It asserts the line spans of all three blocks and that both inner blocks have the outer block as their parent.
- `unfinished_directives_retain_their_body_and_leave_the_outer_closer_outside` nests a 3-colon `tip` block inside a 6-colon `note` block. It checks that the inner block's byte range does not include the outer 6-colon closer.
- `empty_long_closed_and_quoted_directives_keep_original_unicode_offsets` covers nesting inside a blockquote, with CRLF line endings and Unicode text.
- `two_colons_and_inline_directive_text_do_not_open_containers` covers the lower bound. A two-colon `:: {note}` opener, an invalid `:::{ }` opener, and `Text :::{note}` mid-line create no block, and a bare `:::` opens no block.

**Closer length and trailing content**
- In `nested_fence_lengths_and_closer_whitespace_preserve_the_right_containers`, a 3-colon line does not close the 4-colon inner block. A `:::: trailing text` line does not close it either. `::::   ` with trailing whitespace does close it. These cases give the exact line ranges for the inner block, so the "at least as many colons" rule, the "only whitespace" rule and the too-short case are all asserted.
- `empty_long_closed_and_quoted_directives_keep_original_unicode_offsets` covers a closer with more colons than the opener (`:::{note}` closed by `:::::`) and equal-length closers.
- The unfinished and unclosed cases are covered by `unfinished_directives_retain_their_body_and_leave_the_outer_closer_outside` and by the `:::{note}` source with no closer.

**Backtick and tilde code fences shield colon directives**
- `literal_code_inline_code_and_html_shield_directive_looking_text` uses a 4-backtick fence holding a 3-backtick line, and a 4-tilde fence holding a 3-tilde line. Each source yields exactly one block and no paragraph.
- It also covers a ```` ```{note} ```` directive fence whose body contains `:::{tip}`.
- The nested-fence test also puts `::::::` and `:::{fake}` inside a `~~~` fence. The line inside that fence is owned by the outer block, so no extra block appears.
- The CommonMark fence rules are delegated to the tree-sitter markdown parser. The tests exercise the length, character and shielding behaviour that matters here. Mismatched fence characters and unclosed code fences are not tested directly. I did not count those as gaps because the requirement does not single them out.

**Inline code and raw HTML**
- `literal_code_inline_code_and_html_shield_directive_looking_text` covers a multi-line inline code span, a `<div>` HTML block, an HTML comment, and single-line `` `:::{note}` ``. It asserts that none of them produces a block.

The assertions are on block counts, line spans, parents and byte ends, so they would catch wrong behaviour in each of these cases. No `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.

text: Colon directive fences use three or more colons and support nested directives
with shorter inner fences. A colon-only closing fence has at least as many
colons as its opener, followed only by optional whitespace.
Backtick and tilde code fences follow CommonMark rules and shield their contents
from colon-directive recognition. Fence-like text in inline code or raw HTML
Colon-fenced directives and fenced code blocks have anonymous `block` nodes
A block contains its opening fence, body, and closing fence when present.
Its parent is the nearest enclosing outline container.
An unclosed colon fence retains its block through the end of the enclosing
file or directive body, excluding the enclosing directive's closing fence.
Colon-fenced directive bodies are outlined recursively as Markdown. Ordinary
fenced code-block contents remain literal, creating no nested paragraph or
directive nodes. Backtick fences with a directive name such as `{note}` in
their info string are literal code blocks.
